summary: 60-foot Aermotor LS40 tower built 1928 on Mount Irvine in Allegany State Park; moved to Science Hill, taken down, and reassembled at an Ellicottville BOCES school.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia and the Southern Tier Mount Irvine entry say 1931; the Southern Tier Science Hill entry says 1932. The story gives 1931 and reports the 1932 date.
Wikipedia and the Southern Tier list say 1978; the Allegany State Park article says park personnel took it down in the early 1970s. The story reports both and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Core facts agree across Wikipedia, the Southern Tier list and the Allegany State Park article: 1928 build by the Division of State Parks as a 60-foot Aermotor LS40, park staffing only in high fire danger, reassembly by an Ellicottville BOCES class. Two dates conflict (move 1931 vs 1932; takedown 1978 vs early 1970s); both are reported in the story. No source read describes the Mount Irvine summit today or whether the reassembled tower still stands at Ellicottville, so no current-remains claim is made. Access is left unset: the summit is inside Allegany State Park, but no source describes access to the old site. The location (highest point between the headwaters of Rice Brook and South Carrollton Creek) is from the Southern Tier list and is now quoted as evidence [2]; the Facebook snippet that places the original tower at Rice Brook near Thunder Rocks was not readable, so it is not used. Brief check: status gone, kind tower and coordinates (42.06283, -78.66767) match FFLA; Wikipedia's coordinates (42.062841, -78.667529) agree. staffing as_of 1931 marks the start of the arrangement the sources describe; no end date is given.
